Unmodified 64-bit source, header and license from Ilya Grebnov's [libsais v2.10.4](https://github.com/IlyaGrebnov/libsais/tree/ce90878d784b5ff7d019300535675e4a2e22aae0), commit `ce90878d784b5ff7d019300535675e4a2e22aae0`. `src/libsais64.c` SHA-256 `7bc8ad09c728b36f4791aa8091101f5c67086b1f1f1636fea49b2dd7cea255f6`; `include/libsais64.h` `210efb56cc0952c7412c257c3b27bd04b4e126df1abdf03c63eecdf702f9b6e0`. Apache-2.0, see LICENSE. Upstream's `src/libsais.c` and `include/libsais.h` at this commit are byte-identical to the already vendored `token-libsais.{c,h}`. Compile against that header, without OpenMP; no changes to the frozen C++ path. On lengths <= INT32_MAX, the byte API uses the upstream narrow kernel and expands its result into the 64-bit SA. A forced small test checks the ABI, output width and consumer, **not** native >INT32_MAX performance. We use the byte dictionary API only; the recursive integer-parse residual is still unintegrated.
